banlist_most_defensible.summary: Ambiguities in the official banned/restricted list use the reading recorded by the official-sources review.
banlist_most_defensible.rationale: The list's wording leaves these points open; the chosen reading is the conservative one for tournament-style validation and is reported in validation messages.

canonical_printing.summary: When printings of one card number differ, every printing uses the gameplay fields of one canonical printing.
canonical_printing.rationale: Cards with the same card number are the same card (2-1-1). The base printing on the official card list carries Bandai's current wording: in this snapshot every printing whose gameplay wording differs from it is an Edition Beta, event/promotional, bonus-pack or same-set parallel print, while every later reprint (SC01 Deck Build Box, GD05 reprints, 2026 prize prints) matches it up to reminder text and line order. A later reworded reprint therefore supersedes the older wording.

edition_beta_superseded.summary: Edition Beta printings whose stats or text deviate are superseded by the standard printing.
edition_beta_superseded.rationale: Edition Beta was a pre-release product; its deviating records are superseded rewordings or data errors. Whether Edition Beta cards are tournament-legal is decided by the official tournament rules (see data/official), not here.

engine_derives_markers.summary: keyword_effects/timing_markers are search aids; the engine derives keywords and timings from the effect text.
engine_derives_markers.rationale: gcg-api extracts them with a fixed vocabulary that drops 【Pilot】, <Development>, Pilot qualifications and the Activate･Main/Action pairing, and lists keywords a card merely mentions.

errata_supersedes_print.summary: Official errata replace the printed text: gcg-api applies most of them, a field_override applies any the snapshot lacks, and each run re-verifies both.
errata_supersedes_print.rationale: Errata are Bandai's official corrections. gcg-api usually applies them to every printing; a field_override covers an erratum gcg-api has not shipped yet (errata-unapplied:*), and the detector fails loudly if a refresh loses one.

faq_clarifies_rules.summary: Official rules-FAQ answers clarify or fill gaps in the comprehensive rules and are followed as written.
faq_clarifies_rules.rationale: The rules FAQ is published with the rules by Bandai; tests tagged @pytest.mark.faq pin each answer.

most_defensible_reading.summary: Genuinely ambiguous text gets the most defensible reading, with the reasoning recorded in the resolution.
most_defensible_reading.rationale: No official source settles the question; the chosen reading follows the closest rules, rulings and FAQ answers so that later official clarification is easy to adopt.

null_stat_is_zero.summary: A stat the rules require but the card data leaves empty is 0.
null_stat_is_zero.rationale: Every Unit and Base has AP (3-2-5, 3-5-4) and the official list shows no value for these cards; 0 is the only value consistent with a blank and with 1-3-6.

rules_obvious_reading.summary: Typos and undefined wording in the rules take their obvious meaning, consistent with the rest of the rules.
rules_obvious_reading.rationale: Another rule or an official FAQ states the same thing unambiguously.

rules_xref_intended_target.summary: A wrong cross-reference in the rules is read as a reference to the section it obviously means.
rules_xref_intended_target.rationale: Cross-references carry no rules content of their own; the cited title (or topic) identifies the intended section unambiguously.

ruling_overrides_text.summary: Official card rulings override or complete the literal card text and the comprehensive rules.
ruling_overrides_text.rationale: Rulings are Bandai's authoritative answers for that card; the same reading is applied to identical wording on other cards. The engine implements the ruled behaviour and a test tagged @pytest.mark.ruling pins it.

text_format_correction.summary: Obvious formatting defects in the card text are corrected with field_overrides at load time.
text_format_correction.rationale: The defect would make a template compiler misread the card (missing keyword brackets, ASCII ':' as cost separator); the correction restores the standard template without changing meaning.

token_stats_from_effect.summary: A token's stats come from the effect that creates it; token card records are informational.
token_stats_from_effect.rationale: Effects specify tokens in full, e.g. [Gundam]((White Base Team)･AP3･HP3); the standard token cards match those specs while some Edition Beta token records do not.

evidence.quote: When the HP of a Unit, Base, or Shield becomes zero less after receiving damage
A card that receives damage equal to or greater than its HP is destroyed as a result of rules management.

resolution.decision: Read 11-3-1 as 'becomes zero or less': destroyed when damage ≥ current HP.
resolution.rationale: 5-5-2 states the same rule unambiguously.

conflicts.title: Bases 'have AP' and seemingly deal battle damage, but no Base has AP
conflicts.description: 3-5-4/3-5-4-1 say Bases have AP used in battle and 13-1-5-2 speaks of battle damage 'from the Unit or Base targeted for attack', yet 8-5-2-4 has only the attacker deal damage to a Base, the attack target is always the player (8-2-1), the EX Base has 0 AP (5-17-3-1-1) and every Base record has no AP (see data-null:BASE:ap).

evidence.quote: Bases have AP and HP.
AP shows a Base’s offensive strength in battle.
battle damage from the Unit or Base targeted for attack is not received
If there is a Base in the enemy shield area, the attacking Unit deals an amount of battle damage equal to its AP to the Base targeted for attack.
An EX Base is a Base token with 0 AP and 3 HP.

resolution.decision: Bases have 0 AP and never deal battle damage; an attack on a player with a Base present deals the attacker's AP to the Base only (excess is lost, 5-5-6); <First Strike> changes nothing against a Base.
resolution.rationale: Every printed Base lacks AP and 8-5-2-4 describes one-way damage; 13-1-5-2's mention of a Base dealing damage has no card that could use it.

conflicts.title: 'Remove', 'removed from the game' and 'exile' are used inconsistently
conflicts.description: 5-12-1 defines 'remove' as placing a card into the removal area, 5-17-4 says tokens 'removed from the game' go outside the game, 5-17-3-2-3 says a used EX Resource is 'removed from the game', 13-1-8-1 and many cards say 'exile … from the game' (never defined), and EX Resource reminder text says it is 'exiled from the game'.

evidence.quote: This describes a card being placed from any location into the removal area.
Tokens removed from the game are placed outside the game, and not in the removal area.
When an EX Resource is used to pay a cost, that EX Resource is removed from the game.
you may exile (number) of (G Generation) cards in your trash from the game
(Rest an EX Resource then exile it from the game when paying a cost.)
When one of your EX Resources is exiled from the game, you may choose 1 of your Units. During this turn, when it receives enemy damage, reduce it by 3.

resolution.decision: 'Exile (from the game)', 'remove' and 'removed from the game' all mean: a card goes to its owner's removal area; a token (including EX Resources/EX Bases) instead leaves the game. An EX Resource used to pay a cost is 'exiled' for GD05-018's trigger.
resolution.rationale: Card rulings Q194/Q211/Q213/Q220/Q226/Q229/Q232 place exiled cards in the removal area 'not including tokens', and 5-17-4 keeps tokens out of it.

conflicts.title: 【When Linked】 triggers when a linking Pilot is 'set'
conflicts.description: 13-2-11-1 defines 【When Linked】 as activating 'when a pilot that meets the link condition is set'; 'set' is not a defined term (pairing is 5-9).

evidence.quote: is a keyword that indicates an effect activates when a pilot that meets the link condition is set.
This describes placing a Pilot card, or a Command card with a 【Pilot】 effect, beneath a Unit.

resolution.decision: 【When Linked】 triggers when a Pilot that satisfies the Unit's link condition is paired with it (by playing or by an effect, ruling Q184); it does not trigger when an existing pairing later starts to satisfy the condition.
resolution.rationale: 'Set' is the only placement verb used for Pilots here and pairing is the only way a Pilot is placed beneath a Unit.

conflicts.title: A 0-AP attack on a player with no shield-area cards

Damage is not dealt when the amount of damage dealt would be zero.

conflicts.title: EB01-072 Yuu Kajima: every target of a multi-target choice is required
conflicts.description: Card text: “【When Paired】Choose 1 active friendly Unit with <Blocker> and 1 enemy Unit that is Lv.4 or lower. Rest them.” Ruling Q327 (June 12, 2026): “Can I activate this effect and only choose an enemy Unit if I don't have a Unit in play?” — “No. It will only activate if you can choose both Units.” Rule 1-3-2 suggests resolving as much as possible; the ruling applies 10-2-2 to the whole sentence instead.

evidence.quote: 【When Paired】Choose 1 active friendly Unit with <Blocker> and 1 enemy Unit that is Lv.4 or lower. Rest them.
Can I activate this effect and only choose an enemy Unit if I don't have a Unit in play?
No. It will only activate if you can choose both Units.
If a player is required to perform an action and only part of that action is not possible, the player must perform as much of the action as possible.
If an effect requires choosing a target, that effect will not activate if the target cannot be chosen.

resolution.decision: 'Choose 1 X and 1 Y' activates (or the Command can be played) only if both targets can be chosen; it never resolves with just one.
resolution.rationale: Official card ruling Q327 (June 12, 2026) is authoritative for EB01-072; the same reading is applied to identical wording on other cards.

conflicts.title: GD01-001 Gundam: the card itself satisfies 'your Units' references

evidence.quote: All your (White Base Team) Units gain <Repair 1>.
Does this Unit also gain <Repair: 1> from the first effect?
Yes, it does.
Constant effects do not wait to be triggered or activated. They are active from the moment they enter the location where they activate.

No. You cannot activate it if you cannot choose 12 cards.
If a player is required to perform an action and only part of that action is not possible, the player must perform as much of the action as possible.

resolution.decision: An effect that chooses N cards from a public location activates only if N valid cards can be chosen; no partial resolution.

Since the block is already established, the two Units continue their battle.

If I destroy a damaged Link Unit with an effect that says to "destroy" a Unit, does this effect activate?
No, it does not.

conflicts.title: GD01-103 The Stubborn Cog: every target of a multi-target choice is required

Rest them.” Ruling Q153 (July 11, 2025): “Can I play this 【Main】 effect and only choose an enemy Unit if I don't have an active Unit in play?” — “No, you cannot.” Rule 1-3-2 suggests resolving as much as possible; the ruling applies 10-2-2 to the whole sentence instead.

evidence.quote: 【Main】Choose 1 active friendly (Earth Federation) Unit and 1 active enemy Unit. Rest them.
Can I play this 【Main】 effect and only choose an enemy Unit if I don't have an active Unit in play?
No, you cannot.
If a player is required to perform an action and only part of that action is not possible, the player must perform as much of the action as possible.
If an effect requires choosing a target, that effect will not activate if the target cannot be chosen.

conflicts.title: GD02-002 Gundam Epyon: a 【Once per Turn】 effect that does nothing is not used up
conflicts.description: Card text: “【During Link】【Once per Turn】During your turn, when one of your Units destroys an enemy Unit with battle damage, set this Unit as active.” Ruling Q197 (January 09, 2026): “While this Unit is active, another one of my Units destroys an enemy Unit with battle damage. At this time, does this Unit get set as active and the effect end up activated?” — “No. The Unit is already active, so setting it as active is not performed and the effect does not end up activated. This means its once per turn activation has not occurred at this time.” Choosing a target does not require the action to change anything.

While this Unit is active, another one of my Units destroys an enemy Unit with battle damage. At this time, does this Unit get set as active and the effect end up activated?
No. The Unit is already active, so setting it as active is not performed and the effect does not end up activated. This means its once per turn activation has not occurred at this time.
If you are required to put an entity into some state that entity is already in, the entity remains in the state it was in, and the action putting it into that state is not performed.

resolution.decision: If a 【Once per Turn】 effect resolves without performing its action (e.g. setting an already-active Unit active), it does not count as activated for 【Once per Turn】 and may trigger again this turn.
resolution.rationale: Official card ruling Q197 (January 09, 2026) is authoritative for GD02-002; the same reading is applied to identical wording on other cards.

evidence.quote: 【Deploy】Choose 1 other active friendly (Clan) Unit. Rest it. If you do, choose 1 enemy Unit with 2 or less AP. Deal 2 damage to it.
For this effect, do I have to choose a friendly Unit if there is one it can choose in play even when there are no enemy Units with 2 or less AP in play?

those targets are chosen at the point in time when the instructions appear in the effect.

resolution.decision: Triggered effects choose targets sentence by sentence: an available first target must be chosen (and the action performed) even if a later 'If you do' target does not exist. (Commands differ: 10-1-8-1-2.)
resolution.rationale: Official card ruling Q223 (January 16, 2026) is authoritative for GD03-039; the same reading is applied to identical wording on other cards.

conflicts.title: GD03-049 Gundam Exia (Trans-Am): HP comparisons use current HP

Destroy it.” Ruling Q224 (January 16, 2026): “When choosing a Unit with the lowest HP for this second effect, do I look at the base HP or the current HP that is reduced by damage and such?” — “Choose a Unit with the lowest current HP.” The FAQ (Q96) and this ruling define HP references as HP after damage.

evidence.quote: When this Unit destroys an enemy shield area card with battle damage, if there are 10 or more (CB) cards in your trash, choose 1 enemy Unit with the lowest HP. Destroy it.
When choosing a Unit with the lowest HP for this second effect, do I look at the base HP or the current HP that is reduced by damage and such?
Choose a Unit with the lowest current HP.

resolution.decision: Every HP reference in card text (filters, 'lowest HP') uses current HP = modified HP minus damage.

conflicts.title: GD03-072 Aile Strike Gundam: scope of 'If …' / 'If you do' over a following 'Then'

evidence.quote: 【Deploy】If you have another (Triple Ship Alliance) Unit in play, draw 1. Then, discard 1.
For this second effect, do I have to discard one card even if I don't have a (Triple Ship Alliance) Unit in play?
No. It won't activate if you don't have a (Triple Ship Alliance) Unit in play, so you don't have to discard.
Even if the text portion preceding the word “Then” in card text text cannot be resolved, resolving the succeeding portion is possible.

resolution.decision: A leading 'If <condition>,' or 'If you do,' governs every following sentence joined by 'Then' in the same effect; 'Then' only makes the next part independent of whether the immediately preceding action succeeded.
resolution.rationale: Official card ruling Q233 (January 16, 2026) is authoritative for GD03-072; the same reading is applied to identical wording on other cards.

conflicts.title: GD03-074 Tieren Taozi: forced attack-target effects

evidence.quote: 【During Pair】While you have another (Superpower Bloc) Unit in play, enemy Units choose this rested Unit as their attack target if possible when attacking.
What happens if there are multiple Units in play that attract the attack target with effects like "Enemy Units choose this rested Unit as their attack target if possible when attacking"?
Choose one of the Units attracting the attack target as the attack target.

resolution.decision: When declaring an attack: 'must choose that Unit' (GD04-107) outranks 'choose … if possible' attractors; with several eligible forced/attracting Units the attacker picks one; a forced Unit that is not a legal target (active without an active-target permission, or gone) imposes nothing; constraints apply at declaration only and never retarget an attack in progress.
resolution.rationale: Official card ruling Q234 (January 16, 2026) is authoritative for GD03-074; the same reading is applied to identical wording on other cards.

conflicts.title: GD03-079 G-Defenser: substitution needs the original option
conflicts.description: Card text: “When you rest your Base with one of your Units' effects, you may rest this Unit instead.” Ruling Q425 (July 10, 2026): “If I have this Unit and GD02-069 Zeta Gundam in play but there are no friendly Bases in play, can Zeta Gundam rest this Unit instead of a Base and activate its 【Activate･Main】 effect?” — “No, it cannot. When you rest your Base, this effect enables you to rest the Unit instead, so if the prerequisite Base isn't present, the Unit cannot be rested in place of it.” The rulings confirm a substitute can only replace an action that could have been performed.

evidence.quote: When you rest your Base with one of your Units' effects, you may rest this Unit instead.
If I have this Unit and GD02-069 Zeta Gundam in play but there are no friendly Bases in play, can Zeta Gundam rest this Unit instead of a Base and activate its 【Activate･Main】 effect?
No, it cannot. When you rest your Base, this effect enables you to rest the Unit instead, so if the prerequisite Base isn't present, the Unit cannot be rested in place of it.
When some event would occur, a substitution effect replaces the implementation of that event with another event.

resolution.decision: 'Rest X instead' may replace resting a Unit/Base only if that Unit/Base could have been rested, and replaces exactly one of them.

Can I draw a card if the Unit chosen for this 【Deploy】 effect battles and both Units are destroyed?
Yes, you can.
If both battling Units are destroyed, their destruction is treated as happening simultaneously.
If a card with a triggered effect leaves the location where it is active while that effect is waiting to be activated after it was triggered, the effect still activates.

conflicts.title: GD05-003 Waldfeld's Murasame: 【Destroyed】 conditions use the last known state

evidence.quote: When one of your EX Resources is exiled from the game, you may choose 1 of your Units. During this turn, when it receives enemy damage, reduce it by 3.

It only checks for destruction by an effect that reads "destroy it" or similar.” The rules use 'destroy' for both damage and effect destruction; rulings separate them.

evidence.quote: 【Once per Turn】When one of your Units is destroyed by an effect, draw 1.
If one of my Units is destroyed by effect damage, does this card's second effect activate?
No, it does not. It only checks for destruction by an effect that reads "destroy it" or similar.
This describes cards receiving damage equal to or greater than their HP and cards being placed from the field into the trash by effects.

resolution.decision: Record the cause of every destruction (battle damage, effect damage, 'destroy' effect, rules). 'Destroyed by an effect' / 'can't be destroyed by effects' mean 'destroy' effects only; 'destroyed with damage' means battle or effect damage; 'with battle damage' means battle damage only.
resolution.rationale: Official card ruling Q368 (July 10, 2026) is authoritative for GD05-054; the same reading is applied to identical wording on other cards.

conflicts.title: GD05-057 Gyunei's Jagd Doga: scope of 'If …' / 'If you do' over a following 'Then'
conflicts.description: Card text: “【Activate･Main】【Once per Turn】Choose 1 of your other Units. Destroy it. If you do, set this Unit as active. It can't choose the enemy player as its attack target during this turn.” Ruling Q371 (July 10, 2026): “If this Unit is active, can I destroy one of my Units with its 【Activate･Main】 effect?” — “Yes, you can, and since you perform as much of the effect as possible following "If you do," it can't choose the enemy player as its attack target during this turn.” Read literally, 5-20-2 lets the 'Then' part resolve on its own; the ruling puts it inside the preceding condition.

evidence.quote: 【Activate･Main】【Once per Turn】Choose 1 of your other Units. Destroy it. If you do, set this Unit as active. It can't choose the enemy player as its attack target during this turn.
If this Unit is active, can I destroy one of my Units with its 【Activate･Main】 effect?
Yes, you can, and since you perform as much of the effect as possible following "If you do," it can't choose the enemy player as its attack target during this turn.
Even if the text portion preceding the word “Then” in card text text cannot be resolved, resolving the succeeding portion is possible.

resolution.decision: A leading 'If <condition>,' or 'If you do,' governs every following sentence joined by 'Then' in the same effect; 'Then' only makes the next part independent of whether the immediately preceding action succeeded.
resolution.rationale: Official card ruling Q371 (July 10, 2026) is authoritative for GD05-057; the same reading is applied to identical wording on other cards.

conflicts.title: GD05-060 Gundam Flauros (Ryusei-Go): '【Deploy】/【Attack】' means both timings
conflicts.description: Card text: “【Deploy】/【Attack】Choose 1 enemy Unit that is Lv.2 or lower. Destroy it.” Ruling Q372 (July 10, 2026): “Does 【Deploy】/【Attack】 activate the effect during both the 【Deploy】 and the 【Attack】 timing?” — “Yes, that is correct.” '/' between timings means the effect has both timings.

evidence.quote: 【Deploy】/【Attack】Choose 1 enemy Unit that is Lv.2 or lower. Destroy it.
Does 【Deploy】/【Attack】 activate the effect during both the 【Deploy】 and the 【Attack】 timing?
Yes, that is correct.
It performs the same function as the conjunction “or” would in those situations.

resolution.decision: '【A】/【B】' gives the effect both timings; each triggers independently (no shared once-per-turn).
resolution.rationale: Official card ruling Q372 (July 10, 2026) is authoritative for GD05-060; the same reading is applied to identical wording on other cards.

conflicts.title: GD05-061 Geara Doga: block stands after <Blocker> is lost
conflicts.description: Card text: “While you have another (Neo Zeon) Unit in play, this Unit gains <Blocker>.” Ruling Q374 (July 10, 2026): “With the conditions for its effect fulfilled, this Unit gains <Blocker> and blocks an enemy Unit. After that, the conditions become unfulfilled and it loses <Blocker>. At this time, what happens to this Unit's block?” — “Since the block is already established, the two Units continue their battle.” The rules do not say what happens to an established block when the blocker later loses <Blocker>.

evidence.quote: While you have another (Neo Zeon) Unit in play, this Unit gains <Blocker>.

With the conditions for its effect fulfilled, this Unit gains <Blocker> and blocks an enemy Unit. After that, the conditions become unfulfilled and it loses <Blocker>. At this time, what happens to this Unit's block?
Since the block is already established, the two Units continue their battle.
When activated, this effect changes the attack target of the attacking Unit to the Unit with <Blocker>.

resolution.decision: Once <Blocker> has changed the attack target, the new target stays the attack target for the rest of the battle even if the blocker loses <Blocker>.
resolution.rationale: Official card ruling Q374 (July 10, 2026) is authoritative for GD05-061; the same reading is applied to identical wording on other cards.

conflicts.title: GD05-068 Shining Gundam (Super Mode): activating 【Main】 of a paired Command
conflicts.description: Card text: “When you activate a (Special Move) Command's 【Main】/【Action】, this Unit gains <Suppression> during this turn.” Ruling Q376 (July 10, 2026): “Does this card's first effect activate even when I use an effect like GD05-035 Dragon Gundam's to activate 【Main】 on a (Special Move) Command card paired with a Unit?” — “Yes, it does.” 3-4-4 would send the Command to the trash; the rulings keep it paired and make the activation free.

evidence.quote: When you activate a (Special Move) Command's 【Main】/【Action】, this Unit gains <Suppression> during this turn.
Does this card's first effect activate even when I use an effect like GD05-035 Dragon Gundam's to activate 【Main】 on a (Special Move) Command card paired with a Unit?
Yes, it does.
If the Command effect portion of a Command card paired as a Pilot is referred to by some effect and that effect activates the Command effect, activate it as a Command effect.
Unless an effect says otherwise, Commands are placed into your trash after their effects have ended.

resolution.decision: Activating 【Main】 on a paired Command (or one discarded by GD05-097) costs nothing, counts as activating that Command's 【Main】 for other triggers, and the paired card stays paired.
resolution.rationale: Official card ruling Q376 (July 10, 2026) is authoritative for GD05-068; the same reading is applied to identical wording on other cards.

conflicts.title: GD05-069 Gundam Maxter: 'destroys an enemy … with battle damage' fires when both Units are destroyed
conflicts.description: Card text: “During your turn, when this Unit destroys an enemy Unit with battle damage, look at the top 4 cards of your deck.” Ruling Q377 (July 10, 2026): “Does this card's first effect activate even when both Units are destroyed in battle?” — “Yes, it does.” The trigger source is itself destroyed in the same damage step; the ruling confirms the trigger still happens and resolves.

evidence.quote: During your turn, when this Unit destroys an enemy Unit with battle damage, look at the top 4 cards of your deck.
Does this card's first effect activate even when both Units are destroyed in battle?
Yes, it does.
If both battling Units are destroyed, their destruction is treated as happening simultaneously.
If a card with a triggered effect leaves the location where it is active while that effect is waiting to be activated after it was triggered, the effect still activates.

resolution.decision: 'When this Unit destroys an enemy … with (battle) damage' triggers even if this Unit is destroyed simultaneously; the pending trigger resolves after both Units are in the trash (parts that need this Unit on the field do nothing).
resolution.rationale: Official card ruling Q377 (July 10, 2026) is authoritative for GD05-069; the same reading is applied to identical wording on other cards.

conflicts.title: GD05-086 Kayra Su: forced attack-target effects
conflicts.description: Card text: “【During Link】Enemy Units other than Link Units choose this rested Unit as their attack target if possible when attacking.” Ruling Q388 (July 10, 2026): “What happens if there are multiple Units in play that attract the attack target with effects like "Enemy Units other than Link Units choose this rested Unit as their attack target if possible when attacking"?” — “Choose one of the Units attracting the attack target as the attack target.” The rules have no notion of forced attack targets; rulings define how they combine.

evidence.quote: 【During Link】Enemy Units other than Link Units choose this rested Unit as their attack target if possible when attacking.

What happens if there are multiple Units in play that attract the attack target with effects like "Enemy Units other than Link Units choose this rested Unit as their attack target if possible when attacking"?
Choose one of the Units attracting the attack target as the attack target.
The attack target can be either the opposing player or a rested enemy Unit.

resolution.decision: When declaring an attack: 'must choose that Unit' (GD04-107) outranks 'choose … if possible' attractors; with several eligible forced/attracting Units the attacker picks one; a forced Unit that is not a legal target (active without an active-target permission, or gone) imposes nothing; constraints apply at declaration only and never retarget an attack in progress.
resolution.rationale: Official card ruling Q388 (July 10, 2026) is authoritative for GD05-086; the same reading is applied to identical wording on other cards.

resolution.decision: Shields are a stack filled from the deck top: the deck's top card is the bottom Shield; the sixth card placed is the top ('first', 'topmost') Shield, damaged and taken first.
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q8 (2025-07-04) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: Player One draws on the first turn
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q15 (2025-07-04): “Can Player One draw a card during the draw phase of their first turn?” — “Yes, they can.” Many card games skip the first draw; this one does not.

evidence.quote: Can Player One draw a card during the draw phase of their first turn?
Yes, they can.
The active player draws one card from their deck and adds it to their hand.

resolution.decision: No first-turn draw skip for Player One.
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q15 (2025-07-04) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: Resource area holds 15 cards in total, at most 5 EX Resources
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q19 (2025-07-04): “Is there a maximum number of cards that can be in the resource area?” — “Yes, there is. Up to 10 Resource cards from the resource deck and 5 EX Resource cards can be placed into the resource area, for a total of 15 cards.” Read alone, 4-4-2 and 4-4-2-1 could allow 15 Resources plus 5 EX Resources.

evidence.quote: Is there a maximum number of cards that can be in the resource area?
Yes, there is. Up to 10 Resource cards from the resource deck and 5 EX Resource cards can be placed into the resource area, for a total of 15 cards.
You may have up to 15 Resources in your resource area.
You may have up to five EX Resources in your resource area.

resolution.decision: At most 15 cards in the resource area including at most 5 EX Resources; a placement beyond either limit is not performed (1-3-2).
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q19 (2025-07-04) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: 【Activate･Main】 on the turn a Unit is deployed
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q30 (2025-07-04): “Can I activate the 【Activate･Main】 effect on a Unit during the same turn it was deployed?” — “Yes, you can.” The deploy-turn restriction covers attacking only.

evidence.quote: Can I activate the 【Activate･Main】 effect on a Unit during the same turn it was deployed?
Yes, you can.
Unless specified otherwise, a newly deployed Unit cannot attack on the turn it is deployed.

resolution.decision: A Unit deployed this turn may use 【Activate･Main】 effects, including rest costs such as <Support>.
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q30 (2025-07-04) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: Player One may attack on the first turn
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q31 (2025-07-04): “Can Player One attack during their first turn?” — “Yes, they can. However, Units cannot immediately attack during the turn in which they are deployed.” No first-turn attack restriction exists beyond the deploy-turn rule.

evidence.quote: Can Player One attack during their first turn?
Yes, they can. However, Units cannot immediately attack during the turn in which they are deployed.
The game begins with Player One’s turn.

resolution.decision: No first-turn attack ban; Units deployed on an earlier turn (none on turn 1) or Link Units may attack.
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q31 (2025-07-04) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: 'Friendly' equals 'your' in 1v1
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q84 (2025-07-04): “Is there a difference between "1 of your Units" and "1 friendly Unit"?” — “There is no difference when playing with 1v1 rules. "1 friendly Unit" means you can choose a teammate's Unit when playing with team battle rules, such as 2v2.” 'Friendly' is only defined in the team-battle rules.

evidence.quote: Is there a difference between "1 of your Units" and "1 friendly Unit"?
There is no difference when playing with 1v1 rules. "1 friendly Unit" means you can choose a teammate's Unit when playing with team battle rules, such as 2v2.
If an effect or such indicates “friendly,” it refers to both your and your teammate’s cards.

resolution.decision: In 1v1, 'friendly' and 'your' select the same cards.
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q84 (2025-07-04) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: AP below zero: clamp only the final value
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q95 (2025-07-04): “A Unit with 1 AP receives the effect "it gets AP-2" then gets AP+3 from another effect after that. At this time, what is the Unit's AP value?” — “It is the result of 1-2+3, or 2 AP.” Clamping after each modifier would give 3 AP in the FAQ's example instead of 2.

evidence.quote: A Unit with 1 AP receives the effect "it gets AP-2" then gets AP+3 from another effect after that. At this time, what is the Unit's AP value?
It is the result of 1-2+3, or 2 AP.
If the result would be negative, treat it as zero unless it will be modified by another effect.

resolution.decision: Sum all AP/HP modifiers onto the printed value and clamp the final result at 0; do not clamp intermediate results.
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q95 (2025-07-04) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: HP in card text means current HP
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q96 (2025-07-04): “When an effect such as "choose 1 enemy Unit with 2 or less HP" references a card's HP, does it reference its current HP?” — “Yes, it does. If the card is damaged, reference its HP after reducing it by that damage amount.” Rules track damage as counters (5-5-1) but never say which HP a text filter reads.

evidence.quote: When an effect such as "choose 1 enemy Unit with 2 or less HP" references a card's HP, does it reference its current HP?
Yes, it does. If the card is damaged, reference its HP after reducing it by that damage amount.
A card with HP is destroyed when that HP becomes zero.

resolution.decision: HP filters and comparisons use current HP (modified HP minus damage counters).
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q96 (2025-07-04) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: Battle damage is damage dealt through AP in a battle
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q97 (2025-07-04): “What is "battle damage"?” — “This is damage dealt by a card's AP, typically during battle.” The FAQ's 'typically during battle' is looser than 5-5-3.

evidence.quote: What is "battle damage"?
This is damage dealt by a card's AP, typically during battle.
This damage is called battle damage.

resolution.decision: Battle damage is only the damage the damage step deals (including battles begun by effects and battle damage redirected by 'instead' effects); effect damage never becomes battle damage even when it equals a Unit's AP.
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q97 (2025-07-04) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: Unqualified 'damage' includes battle damage
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q98 (2025-07-04): “Does the damage mentioned in effects like "when a Unit is destroyed with damage" include battle damage?” — “Yes, it does.” Card text that says just 'damage' covers both kinds.

evidence.quote: Does the damage mentioned in effects like "when a Unit is destroyed with damage" include battle damage?
Yes, it does.
This damage is called effect damage.

resolution.decision: 'Damage' without a qualifier means battle or effect damage.
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q98 (2025-07-04) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: Damage persists between turns
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q99 (2025-07-04): “Does damage received by a Unit disappear at the end of the turn?” — “No, it does not. Damage remains on the Unit in the form of a damage counter.” No rule removes damage at end of turn.

evidence.quote: Does damage received by a Unit disappear at the end of the turn?
No, it does not. Damage remains on the Unit in the form of a damage counter.
Show the current amount of damage a card has received by placing a number of counters equal to that damage on top of it.

resolution.decision: Damage counters stay until recovered or the card leaves the field.
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q99 (2025-07-04) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: 'All your Units get AP+2 during this turn' does not reach Units deployed later
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q105 (2025-07-04): “A new Unit is deployed after the effect "all your Units get AP+2 during this turn" has activated. At this time, does the newly deployed Unit also get AP+2?” — “No, it does not. Effects that bestow some effect on all Units are only applied to Units that were in the battle area at that time.” 10-1-5-7 covers constant effects; resolved effects with a duration are not described.

evidence.quote: A new Unit is deployed after the effect "all your Units get AP+2 during this turn" has activated. At this time, does the newly deployed Unit also get AP+2?
No, it does not. Effects that bestow some effect on all Units are only applied to Units that were in the battle area at that time.
A constant effect with a conditional target is applied the moment a target fulfilling those conditions appears.

resolution.decision: An effect that resolves once and lasts for a duration fixes its affected set at resolution; constant effects (e.g. 【During Pair】 'all your Units get AP+1') keep applying to Units that arrive later.
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q105 (2025-07-04) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: Durations outlive their source
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q106 (2025-07-04): “After an effect which specifies "during this turn" has been activated by an effect such as 【Activate･Main】, the Unit with that 【Activate･Main】 effect is destroyed. At this time, does the effect specifying "during this turn" remain in effect?” — “Yes, it does.” Rules do not say whether a duration ends when its source leaves play.

evidence.quote: After an effect which specifies "during this turn" has been activated by an effect such as 【Activate･Main】, the Unit with that 【Activate･Main】 effect is destroyed. At this time, does the effect specifying "during this turn" remain in effect?
Yes, it does.
Effects with the duration limit “during this turn” lose effect.

resolution.decision: 'During this turn/battle' effects last their full duration even if the card that created them leaves the field.
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q106 (2025-07-04) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: Several new triggers during resolution: active player's first
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q109 (2025-07-04): “Multiple effects activate at the same time and a new effect activates while they are being resolved. At this time, how do players resolve the effects?” — “Give the new effect priority and resolve it. If multiple new effects activate simultaneously, give them priority and resolve them, starting with the active player's effects.” 10-1-6-7 covers one new trigger only.

evidence.quote: Multiple effects activate at the same time and a new effect activates while they are being resolved. At this time, how do players resolve the effects?
Give the new effect priority and resolve it. If multiple new effects activate simultaneously, give them priority and resolve them, starting with the active player's effects.
If a new effect triggers while multiple effects are being resolved, give that new effect priority and resolve it.

resolution.decision: New triggers that occur while a batch resolves form a nested batch resolved before the rest of the outer batch: the active player's new triggers first (in their chosen order), then the standby player's; 【Burst】 still goes first (10-1-6-8).
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q109 (2025-07-04) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: <Suppression>: both Shields leave together before any 【Burst】
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q195 (2026-01-09): “A Shield destroyed by <Suppression> damage is revealed to be a Base card with a 【Burst】 effect. At this time, if I add one of my Shields to my hand for the effect on the Base deployed by the 【Burst】 effect, can I add the second Shield that would be destroyed by <Suppression> to my hand?” — “No, you cannot. The Shields destroyed by <Suppression> are destroyed simultaneously. The Shield you can add to your hand for the deployed Base is the first Shield in your shield area that was not destroyed.” The rules do not say where the second destroyed Shield is while the first one's 【Burst】 resolves.

evidence.quote: A Shield destroyed by <Suppression> damage is revealed to be a Base card with a 【Burst】 effect. At this time, if I add one of my Shields to my hand for the effect on the Base deployed by the 【Burst】 effect, can I add the second Shield that would be destroyed by <Suppression> to my hand?

No, you cannot. The Shields destroyed by <Suppression> are destroyed simultaneously. The Shield you can add to your hand for the deployed Base is the first Shield in your shield area that was not destroyed.
When two Shields are successfully destroyed with this effect, reveal them simultaneously.

resolution.decision: Both Shields destroyed by <Suppression> leave the shield section at once (revealed, pending trash) before any 【Burst】 resolves; 'add 1 of your Shields' then takes the first Shield that was not destroyed.
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q195 (2026-01-09) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: Damage reductions add up
conflicts.description: Rules FAQ Q488 (2026-09-11): “When the effects "reduce damage it receives by 2" and "reduce damage it receives by 3" both activate on the same Unit, is the damage reduced by a total of five?” — “Yes. Reduce the damage by five.” 5-21 does not cover several reductions at once.

evidence.quote: When the effects "reduce damage it receives by 2" and "reduce damage it receives by 3" both activate on the same Unit, is the damage reduced by a total of five?
Yes. Reduce the damage by five.
This refers to decreasing damage a Unit, Base, or Shield receives by the indicated amount before it is received.

resolution.decision: All applicable reductions are summed before damage is received (floor 0, 5-21-2).
resolution.rationale: Official rules FAQ Q488 (2026-09-11) clarifies the comprehensive rules and is followed as written.

conflicts.title: EB01-001 Gundam Astray Red Frame Custom (EX): reading of “It won't be set as active during the start phase of your opponent's ne…”
conflicts.description: Card text: “It won't be set as active during the start phase of your opponent's next turn.”. The wording admits more than one reading. evidence.quote: It won't be set as active during the start phase of your opponent's next turn.

resolution.decision: Only the untap and set-active effects during that start phase (active step and start-step triggers) are prevented. Set-active effects at any other time still work.
resolution.rationale: The text limits the restriction to the start phase (compare rulings ST08-009:Q208 and GD04-102:Q288); a blanket 'can't be set as active' would be broader.

conflicts.title: EB01-003 Narrative Gundam A-Packs (EX): reading of “At the end of your turn, if this Unit is rested, rest all Units. If th…”

evidence.quote: At the end of your turn, if this Unit is rested, rest all Units. If this effect rested 3 or more Units, draw 1.

resolution.decision: The rested check happens at resolution. 'Rested by this effect' means Units that were active just before and are rested afterwards; Units already rested do not count.
resolution.rationale: An 'If' condition is checked when the effect resolves. Resting an already-rested Unit does nothing (rule 1-3-2-1).

conflicts.title: EB01-009 Gundam Full Armor (Thunderbolt) (EX): reading of “All enemy players each choose 1 of their active Units. Rest them.”
conflicts.description: Card text: “All enemy players each choose 1 of their active Units. Rest them.”. The wording admits more than one reading. The effect belongs to its controller, so for the opponent it is an enemy effect whoever does the choosing.

evidence.quote: All enemy players each choose 1 of their active Units. Rest them.

resolution.decision: The opponent makes the choice (Q313). A Unit that 'can't be chosen by enemy effects' cannot be chosen.
resolution.rationale: The effect belongs to its controller, so for the opponent it is an enemy effect whoever does the choosing.

conflicts.title: EB01-017 Haro: reading of “you and the player who destroyed this Unit draw 1”

resolution.rationale: In 1v1, battles are only between Units of opposing players.

conflicts.title: EB01-023 Le Cygne (EX): reading of “All players each look at the top card of their deck. If it is a card t…”
conflicts.description: Card text: “All players each look at the top card of their deck. If it is a card that is Lv.5 or higher, they may reveal it and add it to their hand. They return any remaining card to the top or bottom of their deck.”. The wording admits more than one reading. evidence.quote: All players each look at the top card of their deck. If it is a card that is Lv.5 or higher, they may reveal it and add it to their hand. They return any remaining card to the top or bottom of their deck.

resolution.decision: The active player does the whole sequence (look, optional add, return top/bottom), then the standby player does the same. Each player learns only their own top card.
resolution.rationale: Ruling Q319: players perform it in order starting with the active player, treated as simultaneous.

conflicts.title: EB01-028 Gundam Plutone: reading of “【Once per Turn】When another Unit attacks an enemy Unit, if this Unit i…”
conflicts.description: Card text: “【Once per Turn】When another Unit attacks an enemy Unit, if this Unit is rested, the attacking Unit gains <Breach 2> during this battle.”. evidence.quote: 【Once per Turn】When another Unit attacks an enemy Unit, if this Unit is rested, the attacking Unit gains <Breach 2> during this battle.

resolution.decision: Triggers only for a friendly Unit other than Plutone that attacks an enemy Unit (not the player). The rested condition is checked when it triggers.
resolution.rationale: 'enemy Unit' is relative to Plutone's controller, so the attacker must be friendly. Checking at trigger time (rule 10-2-1) stops an attack made while Plutone is active from using up 【Once per Turn】.

conflicts.title: EB01-036 Darilbalde: reading of “During your turn, all other (G Generation) Units that are Lv.3 get AP+…”
conflicts.description: Card text: “During your turn, all other (G Generation) Units that are Lv.3 get AP+1.”. The wording admits more than one reading. The text says neither 'your' nor 'friendly', and 'all Units' covers both sides elsewhere in the set (EB01-003 ruling Q311, EB01-029).

'Link Unit' uses the linked status at destruction (last known information). It also triggers when this Unit is destroyed in the same damage step, since at that moment it was attacking.
resolution.rationale: Q149, FAQ Q98, and the GD02-093:Q190 resolution for simultaneous destruction (8-5-3-2-3, 10-1-6-4).

conflicts.title: GD02-011 Moebius (Peacemaker Team): which shield-area card is 'battling'?
conflicts.description: “Choose 1 enemy Base/enemy Shield this Unit is battling.” During an attack on a player, 5-22-1 counts 'Bases and Shields in the shield area' as battling without saying which ones.

evidence.quote: 【Activate･Action】Destroy this Unit：Choose 1 enemy Base/enemy Shield this Unit is battling. Deal 6 damage to it.
Any Unit, Base, or Shield taking part in that battle is considered to be battling.
What happens when an attack on a player occurs?
If a Base is present, the Base is attacked. Otherwise, the first Shield is attacked.
After this Unit attacks the opposing player, an enemy Unit blocks and becomes the attack target. At this time, can I activate this Unit's 【Activate･Action】 effect?
No, you cannot.

resolution.decision: While it attacks a player, the Unit is battling exactly the card that would receive its battle damage: the Base if one is present, otherwise the top Shield; only that card can be chosen (6 effect damage). After a block it battles no shield-area card (Q173).
resolution.rationale: FAQ Q32 says the Base, else the first Shield, is what gets attacked.

conflicts.title: GD02-011 Moebius (Peacemaker Team): reading of “Choose 1 enemy Base/enemy Shield this Unit is battling. Deal 6 damage …”
conflicts.description: Card text: “Choose 1 enemy Base/enemy Shield this Unit is battling. Deal 6 damage to it.”. The wording admits more than one reading. Resolution ambiguous:GD02-011:battling-shield plus Q173. With no shield-area card there is no target (10-2-2).

evidence.quote: Choose 1 enemy Base/enemy Shield this Unit is battling. Deal 6 damage to it.

resolution.decision: 6 effect damage goes to the first card of the enemy shield area (DamageShieldArea), so Base immunities and shield-area protections apply. It can be activated only while this Unit is the attacker, the attack targets the player, and the enemy shield area is not empty.
resolution.rationale: Resolution ambiguous:GD02-011:battling-shield plus Q173. With no shield-area card there is no target (10-2-2).

resolution.decision: Triggers when an effect of either player rests this Unit, including resting it to pay an activation cost; attacking and being deployed rested (GD05-026:Q354) do not trigger it.
resolution.rationale: Attacking rests a Unit by the rules, not by an effect; being deployed rested places the Unit in the rested state rather than resting it (Q354).

evidence.quote: all enemy players each choose 1 of their non-battling Units. Destroy them.

conflicts.title: GD05-073 Altron Gundam (EW): reading of “It won't be set as active during the start phase of your opponent's ne…”

resolution.decision: The controller chooses which of the 2 looked cards goes to the bottom; the other stays on top. With only 1 card in the deck, that card is simply returned.

conflicts.title: ST08-001 Ξ Gundam: reading of “【When Paired】Choose 1 enemy Unit with the highest Lv. Deal 3 damage to…”

The wording admits more than one reading. 'At the start of your opponent's turn' fixes when the condition is checked and 'during this turn' sets the duration (rulings Q430, Q431).

evidence.quote: If another friendly (Marine) Unit is in play at the start of your opponent's turn, during this turn, when a friendly shield area card receives enemy effect damage, reduce it by 5.

resolution.decision: Checked at the start of the opponent's turn: if another friendly (Marine) Unit is in play, then for that whole turn enemy effect damage to each of your shield area cards (Base and Shields, including <Breach>) is reduced by 5, even if this Unit leaves play.
resolution.rationale: 'At the start of your opponent's turn' fixes when the condition is checked and 'during this turn' sets the duration (rulings Q430, Q431).

conflicts.title: ST11-009 Kapool: reading of “【Destroyed】If it is your opponent's turn and a friendly (Marine) Unit …”
conflicts.description: Card text: “【Destroyed】If it is your opponent's turn and a friendly (Marine) Unit is in play, draw 1.”. The wording admits more than one reading. Q432 and resolution ruling:ST11-009:Q432: the destroyed Kapool, a printed Marine, counts by last-known information, so the Marine clause always holds.

evidence.quote: 【Destroyed】If it is your opponent's turn and a friendly (Marine) Unit is in play, draw 1.

resolution.decision: Draw exactly when it is the opponent's turn.
resolution.rationale: Q432 and resolution ruling:ST11-009:Q432: the destroyed Kapool, a printed Marine, counts by last-known information, so the Marine clause always holds.

conflicts.title: ST11-012 Loni Garvey: reading of “when it receives battle damage from an enemy Unit, reduce it by 2”
conflicts.description: Card text: “when it receives battle damage from an enemy Unit, reduce it by 2”. The wording admits more than one reading. Only Units deal battle damage (Bases have 0 AP).

evidence.quote: when it receives battle damage from an enemy Unit, reduce it by 2

resolution.decision: For this turn, battle damage from enemy Units to the chosen (Marine) Unit is reduced by 2.
resolution.rationale: Only Units deal battle damage (Bases have 0 AP).

conflicts.title: ST12-012 Ple-Twelve: reading of “Look at the top 2 cards of your deck and return 1 to the top. Place th…”
conflicts.description: Card text: “Look at the top 2 cards of your deck and return 1 to the top. Place the remaining card into your trash. If there is a player with 3 or less Shields, add the card to your hand instead of returning it to your deck.”. The wording admits more than one reading. Rulings Q444 and Q445. This is a 10-1-9 substitution of the destination of the kept card.

evidence.quote: Look at the top 2 cards of your deck and return 1 to the top. Place the remaining card into your trash. If there is a player with 3 or less Shields, add the card to your hand instead of returning it to your deck.

resolution.decision: The player picks which of the 2 cards to keep and the other goes to the trash. The kept card goes to hand if the condition holds, otherwise it stays on top. 'A player' includes yourself and ignores Bases.
resolution.rationale: Rulings Q444 and Q445. This is a 10-1-9 substitution of the destination of the kept card.

conflicts.title: ST12-013 The Final Victor: reading of “You and that player each choose 1 of your own Units. Begin a battle be…”
conflicts.description: Card text: “You and that player each choose 1 of your own Units. Begin a battle between them and only perform the damage step.”. The wording admits more than one reading. 5-22-4 (the first chosen Unit attacks). Both choices precede any Then/If you do (10-1-8-1-1).

evidence.quote: You and that player each choose 1 of your own Units. Begin a battle between them and only perform the damage step.

resolution.decision: You choose first, so your Unit is the attacking Unit (<First Strike> applies to it). Both choices must be possible to play the card.
resolution.rationale: 5-22-4 (the first chosen Unit attacks). Both choices precede any Then/If you do (10-1-8-1-1).

conflicts.title: ST12-015 Two Unicorns: reading of “Choose 1 friendly Unit and 1 enemy Unit that is Lv.5 or higher. Deal 2…”
conflicts.description: Card text: “Choose 1 friendly Unit and 1 enemy Unit that is Lv.5 or higher. Deal 2 damage to them.”. The wording admits more than one reading. Q451's wording ('no friendly Units or no enemy Units that are Lv.5 or higher') matches this reading.

evidence.quote: Choose 1 friendly Unit and 1 enemy Unit that is Lv.5 or higher. Deal 2 damage to them.

resolution.decision: 'Lv.5 or higher' applies only to the enemy Unit.
resolution.rationale: Q451's wording ('no friendly Units or no enemy Units that are Lv.5 or higher') matches this reading.

conflicts.title: ST13-009 Gundam Pharact: reading of “That player chooses 2 Unit cards from their trash. Exile them from the…”
conflicts.description: Card text: “That player chooses 2 Unit cards from their trash. Exile them from the game.”. The wording admits more than one reading. Applies the resolution of GD01-003:Q121 (choosing N cards from a public location needs N) to identical wording.

evidence.quote: That player chooses 2 Unit cards from their trash. Exile them from the game.

resolution.decision: With fewer than 2 Unit cards in that trash, nothing is exiled.
resolution.rationale: Applies the resolution of GD01-003:Q121 (choosing N cards from a public location needs N) to identical wording.

conflicts.title: ST13-012 Suletta Mercury: reading of “When an enemy Unit is destroyed with effect damage while this Unit is …”
conflicts.description: Card text: “When an enemy Unit is destroyed with effect damage while this Unit is attacking, draw 1.”. The wording admits more than one reading. Resolution of Q459: 'destroyed with damage' means battle or effect damage, and 'destroy' effects do not count.

evidence.quote: When an enemy Unit is destroyed with effect damage while this Unit is attacking, draw 1.

resolution.decision: Counts only a destruction by rules management right after an effect's damage step, from any source. It excludes battle damage, 'destroy' effects (Q459) and HP-reduction destruction. 'Attacking' means the current battle's attacker is this Unit.
resolution.rationale: Resolution of Q459: 'destroyed with damage' means battle or effect damage, and 'destroy' effects do not count.

conflicts.title: ST13-013 / ST13-001: 'Deploy 1 to 2 ... Unit tokens'
conflicts.description: The text lets the player pick how many tokens (1 or 2) without saying when the number is chosen.

evidence.quote: Deploy 1 to 2 [Bit / Funnel]((Long-Range Weapon)･AP2･HP2･This Unit can't be paired with a Pilot or attack) Unit tokens.

resolution.decision: The player chooses 1 or 2 first, then that many tokens are deployed simultaneously: with a full battle area, as many Units already in the battle area are trashed (11-4-2-2), and a 'when deployed' trigger fires once for the pair (10-1-6-3).
resolution.rationale: One instruction deploys the tokens, so they enter together; deploying one and then optionally a second would let excess management trash the first token and double 'when deployed' triggers, results the rules cannot produce.

conflicts.title: ST13-015 Operation to Intercept Solomon: reading of “Choose 3 Unit cards from your trash. Exile them from the game. If you …”
conflicts.description: Card text: “Choose 3 Unit cards from your trash. Exile them from the game. If you do, choose 1 enemy Unit. Deal 3 damage to it.”. The wording admits more than one reading. Q121 policy plus 10-1-8-1-1/10-1-8-1-2.

evidence.quote: Choose 3 Unit cards from your trash. Exile them from the game. If you do, choose 1 enemy Unit. Deal 3 damage to it.

resolution.decision: Not playable with fewer than 3 Unit cards in the trash. The enemy Unit is not required to play it (10-1-8-1-2).

conflicts.title: ST14-001 The-O: reading of “Each enemy player's rested Units with the lowest Lv. won't be set as a…”
conflicts.description: Card text: “Each enemy player's rested Units with the lowest Lv. won't be set as active during the start phase of their turn.”. The wording admits more than one reading. The head noun is 'rested Units'. Q462 affects all tied Units, and Q463 limits the freeze to the start phase.

evidence.quote: Each enemy player's rested Units with the lowest Lv. won't be set as active during the start phase of their turn.

resolution.decision: The lowest Lv. is taken among the enemy's rested Units, every tied Unit is affected, and it applies only during the enemy's start phase.
resolution.rationale: The head noun is 'rested Units'. Q462 affects all tied Units, and Q463 limits the freeze to the start phase.

conflicts.title: ST14-006 Full Armor Unicorn Gundam (Destroy Mode): reading of “You may reveal a number of cards equal to the number of enemy players …”
conflicts.description: Card text: “You may reveal a number of cards equal to the number of enemy players among them and add them to your hand.”. The wording admits more than one reading. In 1v1 the number of enemy players is 1 (ambiguous:multiplayer-vocabulary resolution).

evidence.quote: You may reveal a number of cards equal to the number of enemy players among them and add them to your hand.

resolution.decision: May reveal and add exactly 1 card of any type.
resolution.rationale: In 1v1 the number of enemy players is 1 (ambiguous:multiplayer-vocabulary resolution).

conflicts.title: ST14-011 Paptimus Scirocco: reading of “Reduce its AP during this battle by an amount equal to the number of r…”
conflicts.description: Card text: “Reduce its AP during this battle by an amount equal to the number of rested enemy Units.”. The wording admits more than one reading. Consistent with the policy in the resolution of GD01-059:Q135 (conditions and target restrictions are evaluated once, at resolution). A continuously re-counted amount would change after a Blocker rests.

evidence.quote: Reduce its AP during this battle by an amount equal to the number of rested enemy Units.

resolution.decision: The number is counted once, when the effect resolves.
resolution.rationale: Consistent with the policy in the resolution of GD01-059:Q135 (conditions and target restrictions are evaluated once, at resolution). A continuously re-counted amount would change after a Blocker rests.

conflicts.title: ST14-015 Battlefield Emotions: reading of “choose a number of your Resources equal to the number of enemy players…”
conflicts.description: Card text: “choose a number of your Resources equal to the number of enemy players. Set them as active.”. The wording admits more than one reading. In 1v1 the number of enemy players is 1. Choosing an already-active Resource does nothing, and a normal Resource is always the better pick.

evidence.quote: choose a number of your Resources equal to the number of enemy players. Set them as active.

resolution.decision: Sets 1 rested Resource active, normal Resources before EX Resources, without a player choice.
resolution.rationale: In 1v1 the number of enemy players is 1. Choosing an already-active Resource does nothing, and a normal Resource is always the better pick.

conflicts.title: T-014 Ad Balloon: reading of “This Unit can't be set as active or paired with a Pilot.”
conflicts.description: Card text: “This Unit can't be set as active or paired with a Pilot.”. The wording admits more than one reading. The only grammatical reading; it matches the separately printed single-restriction token T-022 ('can't be paired with a Pilot'), and 'can't' beats any permission (10-1-5-6).

evidence.quote: This Unit can't be set as active or paired with a Pilot.

resolution.decision: Two independent restrictions (distributive 'or'). Each is a separate constant rule grant, and 'can't' beats any permission (10-1-5-6).
resolution.rationale: The only grammatical reading; it matches the separately printed single-restriction token T-022 ('can't be paired with a Pilot'), and 'can't' beats any permission (10-1-5-6).

conflicts.title: Old <Breach> reminder text ('this Unit's attack destroys')
conflicts.description: Older printings explain <Breach> as “When this Unit's attack destroys an enemy Unit…” (some even 'a card'), while 13-1-2-1 says 'when this Unit destroys an enemy Unit with battle damage during your turn'. They differ for battles begun by effects and for blocked attacks.

evidence.quote: <Breach 4> (When this Unit's attack destroys an enemy Unit, deal the specified amount of damage to the first card in that opponent's shield area.)
when this Unit destroys an enemy Unit with battle damage during your turn
If an enemy Unit is destroyed in a battle started by this second effect, does that fall within the criterion "when this Unit destroys an enemy Unit with battle damage"?
Yes, it does.

resolution.decision: Apply 13-1-2-1 for every card: <Breach> triggers when, during its controller's turn, the Unit destroys an enemy Unit with battle damage (including battles begun by effects, Q347); reminder wording is ignored.
resolution.rationale: Reminder text has no rules force (2-11-4); newer printings already use the 13-1-2-1 wording.

conflicts.title: 'During this battle' effects created when no battle is in progress
conflicts.description: 【Action】 effects can be used in the end-phase action step, when no battle is in progress. The rules only say when 'during this battle' effects start (8-2-3) and end (8-6-1).

evidence.quote: Effects worded “during this battle” gain effect now.
All effects worded “during this battle” lose effect.
Choose 1 Unit that is Lv.4 or higher. It gets AP+1 during this battle.

resolution.decision: A 'during this battle' effect created while no battle is in progress has no effect; the rest of the effect still resolves.
resolution.rationale: Such effects exist only between 8-2-3 and 8-6-1 of a battle; with no battle there is no period for them to apply, and no reading lets them outlast the turn.

conflicts.title: Multiplayer wording on cards in a 1v1 game
conflicts.description: These texts say 'each/all enemy players', 'number of enemy players', 'enemy team', 'all players' or 'another player'. 12-2-6 defines 'enemy' for multiplayer only; the simulator is 1v1.

evidence.quote: 【Deploy】Look at the top 3 cards of your deck. You may reveal a number of cards equal to the number of enemy players among them and add them to your hand. Return the remaining cards randomly to the bottom of your deck.
If an effect or such indicates “enemy” or “opponent,” it refers to any and all of the other players.
Is there a difference between "1 of your Units" and "1 friendly Unit"?
There is no difference when playing with 1v1 rules. "1 friendly Unit" means you can choose a teammate's Unit when playing with team battle rules, such as 2v2.

resolution.decision: In 1v1: 'enemy player(s)', 'enemy team' and 'another player' mean the opponent; 'the number of enemy players' is 1, so 'if there are 2 or more enemy players' is never met; 'Choose 1 enemy player' chooses the opponent; 'all players each …' is both players, active player first and treated as simultaneous (1-3-4, Q319); ST10-001's 'same enemy player' means it cannot attack the opponent again this turn but may attack rested enemy Units.
resolution.rationale: Direct specialisation of the multiplayer definitions (12-2-6, 12-3-10) to two players.

conflicts.title: Does declining a 'you may' use up 【Once per Turn】?
conflicts.description: 13-2-13-1 limits 【Once per Turn】 effects to one activation per turn, and ruling GD02-002:Q197 says an effect that performs nothing does not end up activated. Neither says what happens when the player declines a 'you may' part of the effect.

evidence.quote: 【Once per Turn】 is the keyword indicating that that effect can only be activated one time during that turn.
If told “you may” perform an effect, you may also choose not to activate that effect.
This means its once per turn activation has not occurred at this time.

resolution.decision: A 【Once per Turn】 triggered effect is used up only if it performs at least one action (including paying a cost). If its target can't be chosen, its 'If' fails, or the player declines its 'you may', it can trigger again this turn. Activated abilities are used up when activated.
resolution.rationale: 10-1-3 treats declining a 'you may' as choosing not to activate the effect, and Q197 treats an effect that performs nothing as not activated; 10-3-3-1: an effect whose target can't be chosen does not activate.

conflicts.title: 'Pay its cost to deploy it': is the Lv. condition checked?
conflicts.description: These effects deploy a card from the trash by paying its cost. 2-9-1 ties the Lv. condition to playing a card, and deploying by an effect is not playing (5-7, 5-8).

evidence.quote: 【Main】Choose 1 Unit card that is Lv.5 or lower from your trash. Pay its cost to deploy it.
The number of resources that are required when playing a card.
Does this effect activate when I pay the cost to deploy a Unit with GD03-051 Gundam X Divider's effect?
Yes, it does.

resolution.decision: Rest active Resources equal to the card's cost as modified where it is (e.g. GD03-058 'This card in your trash gets cost -1'); no Lv. check; if the cost cannot be paid the card is not deployed. The payment counts as paying for the Unit's effect (Q286/Q297/Q400) and the deployed card's 【Deploy】 triggers.
resolution.rationale: Only playing requires the Lv. condition (2-9-1, 7-5-2-2-2); the text asks only for the cost; the level filter printed on each card already limits what can be deployed.

conflicts.title: <Suppression> reminder 'first 2 cards' vs a Base in the shield area
conflicts.description: Reminder text: “Damage to Shields by an attack is dealt to the first 2 cards simultaneously.” 13-1-7-1 applies <Suppression> only when the Unit deals battle damage to an enemy Shield, and 8-5-2-4 sends all damage to the Base when one is present.

evidence.quote: <Suppression> (Damage to Shields by an attack is dealt to the first 2 cards simultaneously.)
deals damage to the first two Shields simultaneously when the Unit with <Suppression> deals battle damage to an enemy Shield in the shield area.
If there is a Base in the enemy shield area, the attacking Unit deals an amount of battle damage equal to its AP to the Base targeted for attack.

resolution.decision: With a Base in the shield area the attack damages only the Base (<Suppression> does nothing, excess is lost). Without a Base, <Suppression> deals the attacker's battle damage to the top two Shields simultaneously (one if only one remains, 13-1-7-3).
resolution.rationale: Reminder text has no rules force (2-11-4); 13-1-7-1 and 8-5-2-4 are explicit.
